lessons.title: Attendance and leave tracker
lessons.mac:
Command D: fill down. Command R: fill right.
Space: tick or untick a checkbox cell.
Six-day week: =NETWORKDAYS.INTL(K2,L2,11,$A$16:$A$21)
(weekend code 11 = Sunday only)

steps.say: This is the leave tracker we'll build. Ten employees, a leave log with approval checkboxes, working days that skip weekends and holidays, each person's balance, and a red flag when someone is running low. HR teams rebuild this every year. You'll build it once.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S21-01 Done

steps.say: In this project you'll use checkboxes, NETWORKDAYS with a holiday list, SUMIFS for balances and a monthly view, and conditional formatting. Practice sheet: S21-01.

acts.t:
In this project
• Checkboxes for approvals (Insert > Checkbox)
• NETWORKDAYS: working days minus weekends and holidays
• SUMIFS: leave taken, balance, leave in a chosen month
• Conditional formatting: low balances in red
Practice sheet: S21-01

steps.say: NETWORKDAYS counts working days between two dates, both included. It skips Saturdays and Sundays automatically, and any dates you list as holidays.

acts.t:
NETWORKDAYS(start_date, end_date, [holidays])
start_date: first day of leave
end_date: last day of leave
holidays: a range of holiday dates to skip
Saturdays and Sundays are skipped automatically

steps.say: Here's the layout. Employees in A1 to G11, with yellow columns for us to fill. The selected month in B13. Company holidays for this financial year in A16 to B21. And the leave log from I1 to N21.
Start with approvals. Column N holds TRUE or FALSE. Select N2 to N21, then on the Insert tab click Checkbox. Each TRUE becomes a ticked box and each FALSE an empty one.
Now working days. Click M2 and type equals NETWORKDAYS, open bracket, K2 for the start date, comma, L2 for the end date, comma.
For holidays, type dollar A dollar 16 colon dollar A dollar 21, close bracket, and press Return. The dollar signs lock the holiday list so it doesn't move when we copy the formula down.
M2 shows 2. Ravi took leave from first to fifth October, Thursday to Monday. Saturday and Sunday are skipped, and so is second October, Gandhi Jayanti.
Copy it down. Select M2 to M21 and press Command D.

acts.h: Select M2:M21 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Here's the common mistake. In the scratch cell P2, type NETWORKDAYS with only the two dates and no holiday list.
P2 shows 3, one day too many, because Gandhi Jayanti is counted as a working day. Always pass the holiday list. Delete P2.

Now leave taken this year. Click E2 and type equals SUMIFS, open bracket, dollar M dollar 2 colon dollar M dollar 21, the working days, comma, dollar I dollar 2 colon dollar I dollar 21, the employee IDs, comma, A2.
Add the approval condition: dollar N dollar 2 colon dollar N dollar 21, comma, TRUE, close bracket. Only ticked leave counts. Press Return.
E2 shows 12 days for Ravi. Fill it down: select E2 to E11 and press Command D.

acts.h: Select E2:E11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Balance is quota minus leave taken. In F2 type equals D2 minus E2, press Return, then fill down F2 to F11.

acts.h: Select F2:F11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now the monthly view. G2 counts leave that starts in the month in B13. Type equals SUMIFS with the same three conditions as before.
Then two date conditions on the From column: greater than or equal to B13, and less than or equal to EOMONTH of B13, which is the last day of that month. Close the bracket and press Return.
G2 shows 2 days in October for Ravi. Fill it down from G2 to G11.

acts.h: Select G2:G11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now flag low balances. Select F2 to F11. On the Home tab, open Conditional Formatting, Highlight Cells Rules, Less Than. Type 3 and click OK.
Mohammed Faizal turns red with two days left. That's the person HR should talk to before approving more leave.
Now prove it's live. Click N3, Priya's five-day leave in May, and press Space to untick it. Her leave taken in E3 drops to zero. Press Space again to tick it back.
Change the month. Click B13 and type 2026-08-01. Column G now shows August leave. Then set it back to October.

On a Mac, Command D fills down and Command R fills right. Space toggles a checkbox in Excel for Mac and the web alike. If your company works six days a week, use NETWORKDAYS dot INTL with weekend code 11, which treats only Sunday as off.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Command D: fill down. Command R: fill right.
Space: tick or untick a checkbox cell.
Six-day week: =NETWORKDAYS.INTL(K2,L2,11,$A$16:$A$21)
(weekend code 11 = Sunday only)

steps.say: To recap. NETWORKDAYS with a locked holiday list gives working days. SUMIFS with the approval checkbox gives leave taken, and with two date conditions, leave in any month. Conditional formatting flags low balances.

acts.t:
Recap
• NETWORKDAYS(start, end, $holidays$)
• SUMIFS with TRUE for approved leave; add date conditions for a month
• Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than to flag low balances

steps.say: Your challenge: add column O with working days for a six-day week using NETWORKDAYS dot INTL, and check Ravi's October leave by hand. Compare with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In O2: =NETWORKDAYS.INTL(K2,L2,11,$A$16:$A$21), fill down.
Ravi, 1 to 5 Oct: Thu, Sat, Mon (Fri is a holiday) = 3.
Compare with sheet S21-01 Done.

lessons.title: Payroll with PF, ESI and TDS
lessons.mac:
Command D: fill down. Tab: next cell.
Control + ` : show formulas (press again to hide).
Data > Data Validation works the same in Excel for Mac.

steps.say: This is the payroll sheet we'll build for ten employees. Gross pay, PF with the fifteen-thousand-rupee wage ceiling, ESI for lower salaries, professional tax, a monthly TDS estimate, net pay and employer costs. Below it, a payslip that fills itself when you pick an employee ID.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S21-02 Done

steps.say: In this project you'll write the earnings and deductions formulas, a simple TDS estimate with a slab table, and a payslip with nested XLOOKUP and a dropdown. Practice sheet: S21-02.

acts.t:
In this project
• Gross = Basic + HRA + Special allowance
• PF, ESI and professional tax with IF, MIN, ROUND
• TDS estimate with a slab table and SUMPRODUCT
• Payslip: dropdown + nested XLOOKUP
Practice sheet: S21-02

steps.say: Here are the rules we'll use, simplified for teaching. PF is twelve percent of basic, with basic capped at fifteen thousand rupees. ESI is point seven five percent from the employee and three point two five from the employer, only when gross is up to twenty-one thousand.

acts.t:
Rules used (simplified)
PF: 12% × MIN(Basic, ₹15,000), employee and employer
ESI: gross ≤ ₹21,000 → 0.75% employee, 3.25% employer, rounded up
Professional tax: ₹200 if gross > ₹10,000 (state rules vary)
TDS: new regime, ₹75,000 standard deduction, nil up to ₹12 lakh, 4% cess
Always check the current rules before real payroll

steps.say: Open sheet S21-02. Employees are in rows 2 to 11 with basic, HRA and special allowance. The yellow columns F to N are ours. The tax slab table is in P1 to R8.
Gross first. In F2 type equals C2 plus D2 plus E2, and press Tab to move right.
PF in G2: equals ROUND, open bracket, MIN of C2 comma 15000, times twelve percent, comma zero, close bracket. MIN applies the wage ceiling.
ESI in H2: equals IF, open bracket, F2 less than or equal to 21000, comma, ROUNDUP of F2 times point seven five percent comma zero, comma, zero, close bracket. ESIC rounds up to the next rupee.
Professional tax in I2: equals IF, F2 greater than 10000, comma 200, comma zero. Then annual taxable income in J2: equals F2 times 12, minus 75000, the standard deduction.
Now TDS in K2. Start with: equals IF, open bracket, J2 less than or equal to 1200000, comma, zero, comma. Up to twelve lakh of taxable income, the rebate makes the tax nil.

Then the slab tax: ROUND, SUMPRODUCT, open bracket, J2 greater than the slab starts in P2 to P8, times J2 minus those slab starts, times the extra rate in R2 to R8. All three ranges locked with dollar signs.
Finish with: times 1.04 for the four percent cess, divided by 12 for a month, comma zero, and close both brackets. Press Tab.
Net pay in L2: equals F2 minus G2 minus H2 minus I2 minus K2. Then employer PF in M2, the same as G2's formula, and employer ESI in N2 at three point two five percent.
Row 2 is done. Ravi's gross is ₹19,300, PF ₹1,440 and ESI ₹145. Now select F2 to N11 and press Command D to copy all nine formulas down at once.

acts.h: Select F2:N11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Check the edge cases. Vikram in row 6 earns a basic of eighty thousand, but his PF is ₹1,800, twelve percent of fifteen thousand. His monthly TDS is ₹10,487.
Deepa in row 11 has a gross of exactly twenty-one thousand, so ESI still applies: ₹158. And Sneha in row 5 has taxable income just under twelve lakh, so her TDS is zero.
Common mistake: writing the ESI test as less than twenty-one thousand instead of less than or equal to. Deepa would wrongly lose ESI cover. Read the rule, then the formula, word by word.

acts.t:
Common mistake
F2<21000 vs F2<=21000
The ESI limit is “up to ₹21,000”, so 21,000 itself is covered.
Also: forgetting MIN(C2,15000) charges PF on the full basic.

steps.say: Now the payslip. In B17, type equals XLOOKUP, open bracket, dollar B dollar 16, the chosen ID, comma, dollar A dollar 2 colon dollar A dollar 11, comma.
For the return column, use a second XLOOKUP that finds the label in A17 in the header row, A1 to N1, and returns that whole column from A2 to N11. Close both brackets and press Return.
Because the labels in column A match the headers exactly, one formula works for every line. Select B17 to B25 and press Command D.

acts.h: Select B17:B25 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Total deductions in B26: equals SUM of B22 to B25. Net pay in B27: equals B21 minus B26.
For E005, net pay shows ₹1,27,513, the same as L6 in the payroll table. Now a dropdown. Click B16, then on the Data tab click Data Validation.
Set Allow to List, and Source to equals dollar A dollar 2 colon dollar A dollar 11. Click OK.
Pick E008. The whole payslip updates for Kavita: TDS of ₹17,875 and net pay of ₹1,55,125.
On a Mac the same shortcuts apply: Command D fills down, Tab moves right. To check any payroll formula, select the cell and press Control backtick to show all formulas at once.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Command D: fill down. Tab: next cell.
Control + ` : show formulas (press again to hide).
Data > Data Validation works the same in Excel for Mac.

steps.say: To recap. MIN applies the PF ceiling, IF applies the ESI limit, and SUMPRODUCT with a slab table estimates TDS. A nested XLOOKUP with a dropdown turns the table into a payslip.

acts.t:
Recap
• PF: ROUND(MIN(Basic,15000)×12%)
• ESI: IF(Gross ≤ 21,000, ROUNDUP(Gross×0.75%))
• TDS: rebate test + SUMPRODUCT slab tax × 1.04 ÷ 12
• Payslip: dropdown + XLOOKUP(label, headers, table)

steps.say: Your challenge: add a row 28 to the payslip for Cost to company, gross plus employer PF and employer ESI, using the same nested XLOOKUP. Check Ravi's figure by hand.

acts.t:
Challenge
Add “Employer PF” and “Employer ESI” lines to the payslip,
then Cost to company = Gross + Employer PF + Employer ESI.
Check E001: ₹19,300 + ₹1,440 + ₹628 = ₹21,368.

lessons.title: Budget vs actual for the financial year
lessons.mac:
Command R: fill right. Command D: fill down. Command Z: undo.
View > Freeze Panes > Freeze First Column keeps head names visible.

steps.say: This is a budget versus actual report for a full financial year, April to March. Eight expense heads, the variance for every month, the variance percentage for the year, and a status in traffic-light colours. This is the report most finance teams send every month.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S21-03 Done

steps.say: In this project you'll lay out a financial year from April to March, calculate variances with one formula filled across and down, and add a traffic-light status. Practice sheet: S21-03.

acts.t:
In this project
• April to March layout: one block each for Budget, Actual, Variance
• One variance formula, filled right and down
• Variance % and a status: Over, On track, Under
• Traffic-light colours with conditional formatting
Practice sheet: S21-03

steps.say: In India the financial year runs from first April to thirty-first March, so the report starts with April, not January. Keep the three blocks in exactly the same layout. Then one formula works everywhere.

acts.t:
Layout rule
Budget: rows 2 to 11
Actual: rows 14 to 23
Variance: rows 26 to 35
Same columns: B = Apr-25 … M = Mar-26, N = FY total
Variance = Actual − Budget (positive = overspent)

steps.say: Open sheet S21-03. The budget is in rows 2 to 11, actuals in rows 14 to 23. The variance block, rows 26 to 35, is empty and yellow.
Click B27, April salaries. Type equals B15, the actual, minus B3, the budget, and press Return. No dollar signs, because both should move as we copy.
B27 shows ₹51,400. Positive means we spent more than planned. Now select B27 to N27 and press Command R to fill right, all the way to the FY total.
Then select B27 to N34 and press Command D to fill down. Every head and every month now has a variance.

acts.h: Select B27:N34 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Check one. N30 is the FY variance for Travel: ₹232,700. Click it and read the formula: N18 minus N6. The same pattern, just moved.
Now the variance percentage. In O27 type equals N27 divided by N3, the FY budget, and press Return. Fill down to O34.

acts.h: Select O27:O34 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now a status. In P27 type equals IF, open bracket, O27 greater than five percent, comma, quote Over budget quote, comma.
Then a second IF: O27 less than minus five percent, quote Under budget quote, otherwise quote On track quote. Close both brackets, press Return, and fill down to P34.

acts.h: Type IF(O27<-5%,"Under budget","On track")) and press Return
Select P27:P34 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Travel, row 30, is 13.9% over and shows Over budget. The five percent band is a common tolerance. Your finance team may use a different one.
Now the traffic lights. Select P27 to P34. Home, Conditional Formatting, Highlight Cells Rules, Text that Contains. Type Over, keep light red, and click OK.
Same again for On track, and this time choose Green Fill with Dark Green Text.

acts.h: Set with to Green Fill with Dark Green Text

steps.say: And Under budget in yellow. Under budget isn't always good. It can mean a delayed project or an unpaid bill, so it deserves a look too.

acts.h: Set with to Yellow Fill with Dark Yellow Text

steps.say: Common mistake: dividing the variance by the actual instead of the budget. The percentage then changes meaning. Variance percentage is always measured against the plan.

acts.t:
Common mistake
=N27/N15 (÷ Actual) ✗
=N27/N3 (÷ Budget) ✓
Variance % answers: “How far are we from the plan?”

steps.say: Make it dynamic. Change March travel actual, M18, to 200000. The variance, the percentage and the colour all update. Then press Command Z.
On a Mac, Command R fills right and Command D fills down. Command Z undoes. Freeze panes keeps the head names visible as you scroll across the months: View, Freeze Panes.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Command R: fill right. Command D: fill down. Command Z: undo.
View > Freeze Panes > Freeze First Column keeps head names visible.

steps.say: To recap. Lay out April to March with identical blocks. Write one variance formula and fill it right and down. Then add variance percentage, an IF status and traffic-light colours.

acts.t:
Recap
• Same layout for Budget, Actual, Variance
• One formula: =Actual − Budget, fill right and down
• Variance % against budget; IF status with a ±5% band
• Highlight Cells Rules > Text that Contains for colours

steps.say: Your challenge: add a year-to-date view for April to September using SUM over B to G in each block, and a YTD status. Compare the full-year figures with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Add YTD (Apr to Sep) columns: =SUM(B15:G15)-SUM(B3:G3).
Give each head a YTD status with the same IF.
Compare the full-year view with sheet S21-03 Done.

lessons.title: Sales MIS report with AI summary
learn: Copilot or Claude writes the commentary, you check it

steps.say: This is a quarterly sales MIS: KPIs at the top, sales by region, month and category, a chart, and five lines of commentary. The numbers come from formulas. The commentary was drafted by AI and checked line by line.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S21-04 Done

steps.say: In this project you'll build KPIs with formulas on a table, add breakdowns with SUMIFS, create a chart with Copilot, and have Claude draft the commentary, which you then check. Practice sheet: S21-04.

acts.t:
In this project
• KPIs: total sales, invoices, average invoice, top region
• SUMIFS by region, month and category
• Chart by Copilot prompt
• Commentary drafted by Claude, checked by you
Practice sheet: S21-04

steps.say: The data is a table called MISData with one hundred and fifty invoices for July to September 2026. Formulas that use the table name keep working when next quarter's rows are added.
The report area starts at J1. Click K3 and type equals SUM, open bracket, MISData, open square bracket, Net amount, close square bracket, close bracket.

acts.h: Type =SUM(MISData[Net amount]) and press Return

steps.say: In K4, the invoice count: equals ROWS of MISData Net amount. In K5, the average invoice: equals K3 divided by K4.

acts.h: Type =ROWS(MISData[Net amount]) and press Return

steps.say: K3 shows ₹1,54,05,150 from 150 invoices. Now the regions. In K10 type equals SUMIFS, MISData Net amount, comma, MISData Region, comma, J10.

acts.h: Type =SUMIFS(MISData[Net amount],MISData[Region],J10) and press Return

steps.say: In L10, the share: equals K10 divided by dollar K dollar 3. Then select K10 to L13 and press Command D.

acts.h: Select K10:L13 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Top region in K6: equals INDEX of J10 to J13, MATCH, MAX of K10 to K13, comma K10 to K13, comma zero. It returns the region name with the highest sales.
Months next. In K16 type equals SUMIFS, Net amount, Date greater than or equal to J16, and Date less than or equal to EOMONTH of J16. Fill down to K18.

acts.h: Select K16:K18 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Growth in L17: equals K17 divided by K16 minus 1. Fill to L18. Then categories: K21 is SUMIFS on the Category column, L21 the share. Fill both down to row 24.

acts.h: Select L17:L18 and fill down with ⌘ + D
Select K21:L24 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Now the chart. Open Copilot in Edit mode and ask for a clustered column chart of sales by region from J9 to K13, placed next to the report.

acts.t: Create a clustered column chart of Sales by Region using J9:K13 on this sheet, titled Q2 sales by region, and place it to the right of the report starting at column N.

steps.say: Check the chart: four bars, the tallest should be the region named in K6, and the title as asked.
Now the commentary. Open Claude with Control Option C. Ask it to write five short bullet lines of management commentary into J27 to J31, using only numbers that appear in the report.

acts.t: On sheet S21-04, write a management commentary for this Q2 sales MIS as 5 short bullet lines, one per cell in J27:J31. Use only numbers that appear in J1:L24 and cite the cell for each number. Cover total sales, the top region and its share, the month trend, the largest category, and one risk or action. Ask before writing.

steps.say: Claude shows its draft and asks before writing to the sheet. Approve it.

acts.t: Yes, write it into J27:J31.

steps.say: Now check every line. Click J27 to J31 one by one and compare each number with the cell it cites. Look for rounded numbers that changed meaning, and growth figures with the wrong sign.
For example, July sales in K16 are ₹51,73,280 and September in K18 is ₹54,13,030. If the commentary says sales fell in September, it's wrong, and you edit that line yourself.
Common mistake: letting AI add reasons it can't know, like: sales rose because of a new product launch. The data doesn't say that. Delete any cause you can't back with a number or a fact you know.

acts.t:
Common mistake
AI commentary that invents causes:
“Sales rose due to the new launch.” Not in the data.
Keep: what happened (numbers). Add yourself: why (business knowledge).

steps.say: Make it a template. Next quarter, paste the new rows into the MISData table and change the month labels in J16 to J18. Every KPI, breakdown and the chart update. Then ask Claude for a fresh commentary and check it again.

acts.t:
Next quarter
1. Add rows to MISData (the table grows)
2. Update J16:J18 to the new months
3. KPIs, SUMIFS and the chart refresh
4. New AI commentary, checked line by line

steps.say: To recap. Build KPIs and breakdowns with formulas on a table. Let Copilot make the chart and Claude draft the words. And check every number in the commentary against its cell.

acts.t:
Recap
• Table + SUM / SUMIFS / INDEX-MATCH for the numbers
• Copilot for the chart, Claude for the draft commentary
• You check every number and remove invented causes

steps.say: Your challenge: add a sales-executive breakdown with SUMIFS, ask Claude to add one line about the top executive, and check it. Compare the rest of the report with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Add a Sales exec table (6 names) with SUMIFS on MISData[Sales exec].
Ask Claude for one line on the top executive; check the number.
Compare with sheet S21-04 Done.

lessons.title: A simple three-statement financial model
learn: P&L, balance sheet, cash flow linked
Build it, then audit it with Claude
lessons.mac:
Command R: fill right. Command Z: undo.
Control + ` : show formulas; typed numbers stand out.
Control + Option + C: open Claude.

steps.say: This is a three-statement model for Kaveri Home Products: profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow for one actual year and two forecast years, all linked. The check row shows zero, so the balance sheet balances. Claude audited it, and its notes are on the right.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S21-05 Done

steps.say: In this project you'll link profit to retained earnings, cash flow to the balance sheet, add a balance check, and then audit the whole model with Claude. Practice sheet: S21-05.

acts.t:
In this project
• Net profit → retained earnings
• Closing cash (cash flow) → cash (balance sheet)
• A check row that must be zero
• Audit with Claude, then fix what it finds
Practice sheet: S21-05

steps.say: Three links make the statements one model. Profit adds to retained earnings. The cash flow ends with closing cash, which becomes the balance-sheet cash. And assets must equal equity plus liabilities.

acts.t:
The three links
1. Retained earnings = last year's + this year's net profit
2. Balance-sheet cash = closing cash from the cash flow
3. Check: Total assets − Total equity and liabilities = 0

steps.say: Open sheet S21-05. Assumptions are in A3 to B12. The P and L runs from row 14, the balance sheet from row 25 and the cash flow from row 39. Columns C and D are the forecast years.
Most formulas are already in. For example, click C15: revenue grows from last year by the growth rate in B3. Click C19: depreciation is ten percent of last year's fixed assets.
First link: retained earnings. Click C33 and type equals B33, last year's retained earnings, plus C23, this year's net profit. Press Return.
Select C33 to D33 and press Command R to copy it across to the second forecast year.
Now the check. In C37 type equals ROUND, open bracket, C30 minus C36, comma zero, close bracket. Fill it right to D37.

The check isn't zero. This is the classic mistake in a three-statement model: the balance sheet has no cash yet, because we haven't linked the cash flow. An unbalanced check always means a missing or wrong link.
Second link. Click C29, the balance-sheet cash, and type equals C49, the closing cash from the cash flow. Press Return, then fill right to D29.
Now C37 and D37 both show zero. The model balances. Cash at the end of the first forecast year is ₹22,68,630, and at the end of the second, ₹44,07,675.
Read the cash flow once from top to bottom. Net profit, plus depreciation, less the increase in receivables, plus the increase in payables, gives cash from operations. Then capex and loan repayment.

Now audit with Claude. Open it with Control Option C and ask: audit the model on sheet S21-05. Check the balance sheet balances, closing cash matches balance-sheet cash, and list any typed numbers in the forecast columns. Don't change anything.

acts.t: Audit the three-statement model on sheet S21-05. Check: 1) the balance sheet balances in every year, 2) closing cash in row 49 equals balance-sheet cash in row 29, 3) any typed numbers in the forecast columns C and D that should be formulas, 4) any formula that breaks the pattern of its row. Cite cells. Do not change anything.

steps.say: Claude reports on each check with cell citations. It should confirm the balances and point out that D18, the second-year operating expenses, is a typed number.
Check that yourself. Click D18. The formula bar shows a plain number, while C18 is a formula. Today the value happens to be right, but if you change the growth rate, D18 won't move.
Fix it by hand. In D18 type equals D15 times dollar B dollar 5, and press Return. The value stays the same and the check stays at zero.
Now a stress test. Ask Claude: if debtor days rise from forty-five to sixty, what happens to cash at the end of FY 2027-28, and does the model still balance? Then test it yourself.

acts.t: On sheet S21-05, if debtor days in B8 rise from 45 to 60, what happens to cash in D29 and does the balance check in row 37 stay at zero? Explain the chain of cells. Do not change anything.

steps.say: Click B8, type 60 and press Return. Cash falls, because customers pay more slowly, but the check stays at zero. That's a well-linked model. Press Command Z to undo.
Common mistake: forcing the balance sheet to balance with a plug, a typed number in cash or equity. The check turns zero, but the model is wrong. Always fix the link, never the check.

acts.t:
Common mistake
Typing a plug to make the check zero.
• A non-zero check = a missing or wrong link
• Usual suspects: cash not linked, net profit not in retained earnings,
  a cash-flow sign the wrong way round

steps.say: On a Mac, Command R fills right, and Control backtick shows every formula so you can spot typed numbers fast. Claude opens with Control Option C.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Command R: fill right. Command Z: undo.
Control + ` : show formulas; typed numbers stand out.
Control + Option + C: open Claude.

steps.say: To recap. Link net profit to retained earnings and closing cash to balance-sheet cash. Add a check row that must be zero. Then audit with Claude, and confirm every finding yourself.

acts.t:
Recap
• Link 1: retained earnings += net profit
• Link 2: balance-sheet cash = closing cash
• Check row = 0 in every year
• Claude audit → you verify → you fix

steps.say: Your challenge: add a dividend of ten lakh rupees per forecast year. It reduces retained earnings and cash. Keep the check at zero. Compare the base model with the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
Add an assumption: dividend ₹10,00,000 per year.
Subtract it in retained earnings (row 33) and as a cash outflow.
The check (row 37) must stay at 0.
Compare the base model with sheet S21-05 Done.

lessons.title: Excel interview questions and answers
learn: Practical tests and how to approach them
